entries.why_wrong: This isn't a complexity problem — `sum_to` never touches an already-computed range twice, so there's no re-scanning to worry about. The real defect is structural: there's no base case to stop the recursion, so it never gets the chance to finish at any complexity.

Python integers grow arbitrarily large and never overflow, so `n - 1` staying valid isn't the issue here. The actual failure is that no call ever returns without recursing further, so the stack itself runs out before any number ever could.

Swapping in multiplication would turn this into a factorial function, not fix a summation — and it still wouldn't stop the recursion. The bug isn't which operator combines `n` with the recursive call, it's that nothing ever returns a value without making another call.
